title: Meta-skill form
description: The questions a meta-skill depends on, as data: stable ids, prompts, probes, time estimates and the profile slots each answer feeds. A consumer can render it as a page (Fluxor), ask it one section at a time (MCP elicitation) or run it as an interview; the repository renders it to Markdown for people. See the meta-skills contract (meta-skills.md, beside catalog-format.md).

formVersion.description: SemVer of the form. Adding a question is a minor bump; changing what a question id asks, or removing one, is a major bump, because packs cite questions by id.

role.description: The id of the meta-skill this form belongs to.

title.description: The role's name as people read it ("Backend Engineer").

nameSlot.description: The profile slot that holds the person's name or chosen alias (`engineer_name`). Filled at synthesis, fed by no question.

intro.description: What the interviewer reads before the first question.

wrap.description: What the interviewer does after the last question.

routing.description: How a request reaches this role: lowercase keywords and phrases matched on word boundaries by ceet-autodiscover.

derived.description: Slots synthesized across the whole interview rather than from specific questions (contradictions between answers, for example), with the reason. They count as fed.

profileOnly.description: Slots rendered only in the cognitive profile, never in an artifact template, with the reason. Every other slot must be used by at least one artifact template.

modules.description: Parts of the interview, asked in order. Required modules make the core; optional ones are depth modules the person may skip or do later.

id.description: A letter, unique across the form (`A`, `B`, …, `AA`).
Stable id, cited by packs as `[Q<n>]`. Never renumbered or reused: a new question takes the next free number wherever it is placed.

kind.description: `open`: a direct question. The decision-capture kinds come from cognitive task analysis: `incident` (a Critical Decision Method walk through one real case), `knowledge-audit` (what a novice would miss), `simulation` (thinking through one of the person's real artifacts), `contrastive` (choosing between two concrete options), `limited-information` (deciding with a deliberately partial picture).

required.description: Whether the core needs the answer. An unanswered required question leaves its slots without evidence.

minutes.description: Estimated minutes to answer, follow-ups included.

feeds.description: The profile slots this answer is evidence for (`directives.code_review.philosophy`).

captures.description: What else the answer becomes: `decisions` are real decisions with their rationale, stored as the pack's examples.
